new_statements.quote: ロロ・ポ語の声調は基本的に 55 調、33 調、31 調の 3 種が認められる。現時点のデータからはロロ・ポ語の tone bearing unit は音節である。語声調的な特徴は見られない。また緊喉母音は 33 調および 31 調を持つことが多い。 … このほかに 35 調が特定の形態素に見られることがある。 … 35 調が見られるのは上記のように主に方向や位置関係を表す語彙である。 … 現時点では基本的な声調に含めるとまでは言いがたいが、語彙表を含め、35 調を音素的に表記しておきたい。
new_statements.translation: Lolopho basically has three tones: 55, 33 and 31. On present data the tone-bearing unit of Lolopho is the syllable; no word-tone characteristics are observed. Creaky (tense) vowels mostly carry tone 33 or 31. ... In addition a 35 tone is found on certain morphemes ... mainly words expressing direction and location ... at present it can hardly be counted among the basic tones, but I transcribe 35 phonemically, including in the word list.
new_statements.citation: 林範彦 [Hayashi, Norihiko]. 2015. ロロ・ポ語音論の予備的研究 [A preliminary study of Lolopho phonology]. 地球研言語記述論集 [RIHN Descriptive Linguistics Papers] 7: 171-205. Kyoto: Research Institute for Humanity and Nature.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File on the mirror (sout3129/, 35 pp, text; the PDF's metadata gives the Author 林範彦, created 2015-08-14). chikyu.repo.nii.ac.jp/records/925 confirms 林範彦 'ロロ・ポ語音論の予備的研究', 地球研言語記述論集 7: 171-205, 2015-03-29, RIHN, ISBN 978-4-906888-15-3, file URL answers 302 -> file). Open; a phonology article (phoneme tables, sec. 3.4 tones, 500-item wordlist). | Quote found verbatim at sec. 3.4 声調 p.182-183 of the mirror text (lines 533-535, 557, 566-569; ellipses mark real omissions) and 表1 p.175 '[声調] 55, 33, 31 (35)'. Reading tone / tone language, no stress statement is right: three tones 55/33/31, marginal 35, TBU = syllable, '語声調的な特徴は見られない', nothing on stress. IDENTITY is the problem: the paper never nam…
new_statements.relation_note: Three basic tones 55, 33, 31 (plus a marginal 35 on a few directional morphemes); TBU is the syllable; no word-tone behaviour; creaky vowels mostly carry 33 or 31. Nothing on stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Syllable-tone language with three level/falling tones (55, 33, 31) and a marginal rising 35; no statement about word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: 35 tone restricted to a handful of directional/locational morphemes, possibly morphophonological in origin; creaky vowels favour 33/31.
new_statements.identity_note: Lolopho of Nongbua village, Muang Sing district, Luang Namtha, Laos; speakers report migrating in 2003 from Nyot-U district, Phongsaly, which borders Jiangcheng and Mengla (Yunnan), counties listed for Southern Lolopo [ysp]. Glottolog has no separate Laos-Lolopho languoid (search 'Lolopho' returns only Nanhua/Yao'an/Shuangbo Lolopho, Central Yi). Hayashi himself only links it generically to Chinese Lolopho (Nanhua, Jingdong; Central Yi per Bradley 2000, Lisoish per Lama 2012). Assignment to sout3129 rests on geography (Phongsaly Lolo adjacent to the Jiangcheng/Mengla Southern Lolopo area), not on a stated identification; could instead warrant its own languoid. Wordforms: ȵi31 'two', ȵi33 '2SG', lɔ33 'tongue', gɤ̰31 'give', ŋɐ55ʐo31 'bird'. [name in source: ロロ・ポ語 (Lolopho), ムアンシン方言; autonym in text no. 496 'ŋɔ lo lo pho ŋɐ' = 'I am Lolopho'; pages 171-205 (phoneme table p.174-175; tones sec. 3.4 p.182-183)] | Same Muang Sing (Laos) Lolopho variety and speakers as Hayashi 2015; p.99 explicitly codes it '[Glottocode: lolo1259; ISO 639-3: ycl]' and says Lolopho 'is spoken mainly in Nanhua County and Yao'an County of Yunnan.. and the Phongsaly and Luang Namtha Provinces of Laos'; sec. 6 compares it with two Nanhua [ycl] dialects (Sun et al. 1991: tones 55/33/21; Huang et al. 1992: 55/33/21(13)) and repeatedly notes 'dialectic divergence'. Same ysp-vs-ycl caveat as missed work 1 (source district Nyot-U borders the Jiangcheng/Mengla 'Western Lolo' = ysp zone).

new_statements.quote: The syllable structure of MS Lolopho is C1C2V/T or C1/T. … The tone-bearing unit is the syllable, and there are three main tonemes, namely 55, 33, and 31. A few words denoting directions and some grammatical functions have the 35 tone, which needs further analysis.
new_statements.citation: Hayashi, Norihiko. 2022. A Sketch of the Mammal Terms of Muang Sing Lolopho with Reference to Dialectal Comparison (Topics in Middle Mekong Linguistics 3, Chapter 4). 神戸市外国語大学外国学研究所研究年報 [Journal of Research Institute, Kobe City University of Foreign Studies] 63: 99-125.
new_statements.relation_note: Lexical-semantic study whose sec. 2 'MS Lolopho Phonology' restates Hayashi 2015: Table 1 '[tones] 55, 33, 31 (35)'; syllable structure C1C2V/T or C1/T; TBU = syllable; three main tonemes 55, 33, 31; 35 on a few direction words and grammatical items. Later notes that the animal prefix /ɐ-/ varies in tone (ɐ55-, ɐ33-) with surrounding morphemes (p.111) and that in Loloish a syllable often copies the rhyme and tone of the preceding one (p.104). No stress statement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Three lexical syllable tones 55/33/31 plus a marginal 35; TBU the syllable; no stress rule.
new_statements.exceptions: 35 tone limited to direction words and some grammatical morphemes; prefix ɐ- alternates 55/33 by context.

sources.citation: Zhao, Xiaobao 赵小保. 2025. 彝语岩脚倮倮话的体标记wa33和a33 [The aspect markers wa33 and a33 in Yanjiao Lolo Yi]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen (Minority Languages of China) 2025(1): 120-129. (Author at Dept. of Chinese, Peking University.)
sources.note: Grammar article (perfective wa33 vs imperfective a33). No phonology section: no statement of the tone inventory, sandhi or stress. Tone appears only as Chao tone digits on every cited syllable (values seen: 21, 33, 55, 53), e.g. ŋo33 phi21 dʑa33 wa33 'I have money now', za21 zi33 ʔə55lao55 a33 'he is walking'; footnote: the syllable lao55 has a free variant. States that the only earlier literature on this lect is 赵小保 2019. These are tone MARKS on forms, not a statement.

sources.locator: online appendix B.3 'Spurious Languages; Eurasia', printed pp. s52-s53
sources.note: The only mention of the language in the work. It is an inventory judgement (the Ethnologue entry may be a duplicate of Lolopo [ycl] / Miqie [yiq]), not a linguistic description; no stress, accent or tone information anywhere in the work for this language. The work's five hits on 'tone/tonal' are all bibliography titles about other languages. Wikipedia and hh.bib cite the appendix entry for ysp (identification with Xiangtang, Zhenkang); it will state what documentation, if any, exists.
